overview: This two-page administrative file index concerns electric-power conditions and engineering in Japan from 1940 through the early 1940s. It identifies earlier reports and correspondence on Japan’s electricity shortage, ministerial measures, coal and electric-power supplies, Japanese power systems, and the Toho Electric Power Company, while directing researchers to related decimal-file material and noting the circulation or availability of reports within the U.S. government.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning Japan’s electric-power shortage
subfiles.about: An administrative list entry cross-references Ambassador Grew’s 1940 report on Japan’s shortage of electric power.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records a report from Japan, numbered 4494 and associated with Grew, dated February 15, 1940. The referenced material concerned Japan’s electric-power shortage and included a copy of a ministerial notification and a clipping from Japan Advertisement. Researchers are directed to Sheet No. 4 and file reference 894.50/118.

subfiles.title: List of papers, Sheet No. 4: Electric Power—Japan
subfiles.about: A continuation sheet lists reports and correspondence on Japanese coal supplies, electric-power systems, and the Toho Electric Power Company.
subfiles.summary: The sheet indexes a report from Kobe associated with Sokobin on improvements in Japan’s coal and electric-power supplies. It also notes Federal Power Commission correspondence offering a report on Japanese electric-power systems, while warning that a new edition would have to be prepared because available copies were exhausted. Further entries record J. R. Thomas’s transmission of a report on the Toho Electric Power Company as of April 30, 1942, and a reply stating that copies had been brought to the attention of Department officers.

interest: The file is useful less for substantive technical detail than as a map to dispersed State Department reporting on Japan’s energy infrastructure. It links prewar power shortages and government controls with later assessments of coal supplies, generating systems, and an individual utility company. The note that Federal Power Commission copies were exhausted also reveals contemporary demand within the U.S. government for technical intelligence about Japanese electric power.
